items.title: NEW — a MALFORMED import reports `found 'import' expected an expression` at COLUMN 1 of the statement, whatever the typo (six probes, identical): the import grammar's failure falls back to the expression parser, which points at the keyword — acute once B318's new import forms (`#`, `only`, `(impl T)`, `::*`) multiply the ways an import can be mistyped
items.body: Make the import parser report at the token it stopped on with a curated rule naming the import grammar (one row); pin the six probe shapes; the expression fallback stays for everything that is not `import`-led.

items.title: NEW — `export (helper);` and `export * helper;` compile CLEAN and mean nothing: `parse_export` takes any statement, so an export of a parenthesised expression (or of `*` followed by a name) is accepted silently; zero occurrences in the estate; one curated refusal, shippable today, and the rule B318's `export *;`/`export(in PATH)` grammar needs anyway
items.discussion: paper-visibility-34's F4 and probe P2d (2026-09-13); visibility.md §2.2
items.body: `parse_export` admits a declaration, an `import`/`use`, and (after B318) `*;` / `(in PATH)` — anything else is refused with a steer naming those; one row; pins for the two nonsense forms and the legal controls.

items.title: NEW — `vilan/std/vilan.toml` quotes a STALE census in its prelude comment ('264 names across 59 files'; measured at e4d192e3: 664 top-level declarations across 63 files, 118 of them imported by another std file) — the number B318's brief inherited as '364 unexported'

items.title: NEW — an ANNOTATION-ONLY generic argument carrying a `context` clause is silently INERT at the construction site: `let held: Held<(\|\| void) context current> = Held { body = \|\| print(..) }` inside `current.run(9, ..)`, then `current.run(3, \|\| (held.body)())`, prints `saw 9` (measured) — the clause binds `T` from the VALUE's type and a literal is born clause-less, so the annotation never reaches B309's landing rule; not a miscompile (ordinary capture) but silent; the working spelling is a constructor `fun` whose parameter carries the clause (pinned as `b309_a_generic_argument_carries_the_clause_into_the_field_it_binds`)
items.body: Make the struct-literal field landing consult the annotated EXPECTED type (`seed_tail_expectations` already carries it for an annotated `let`); pin the probe, keep the constructor shape as the control.

items.title: NEW — a `context` clause written in a type position that has NO landing rule (`List<(\|\| i32) context c>`) is admitted and inert: the literal born there captures at creation and the restriction never sees it — sound, silent; a walk-time position gate is the wrong fix (it cannot see through a generic argument, the position B309 wanted)
items.body: A literal-side check in the context pass: 'this literal would be born under a clause the threading cannot follow' — one row; pins for the list element, a map value, and the landing-rule positions as controls.

items.title: NEW — `let x = injected_value;` (UNANNOTATED) is still refused by the value-flow restriction although `x`'s type now carries the clause (B309 moved resolution before the fixpoint) and the threading could follow it; the binding landing rule applies only to an annotated `let`
items.body: Admit the unannotated binding as a forward (the clause comes from the initializer's type); pin it beside the annotated form; the mismatched-clause refusal unchanged.

items.title: NEW — `Option<KeyedCell<K, T>>` as an `[rpc]` return gets only GENERATED-CODE errors: std's macro deliberately does not treat it as a handle (rpc.vl ~5102, 'left to the ordinary Wire refusal') but `handle_return_element` descends through `Option` into `KeyedCell`, so the ordinary Wire refusal stands down and the author reads `in code generated by this attribute: 'Option<KeyedCell<i32, Task>>' does not implement trait 'Wire'`, twice
items.discussion: rpc-34's F1 (2026-09-13); pre-existing, B319 only added the key test
items.body: Decline to descend through `Option` into a KEYED handle (the macro's own rule is `handle_key(inner) == ""`), so the form falls to the Wire refusal in the method's vocabulary; no new row; pin the form and the plain `Option<SignalCell<T>>` control. The alternative — supporting the form with per-key `Absent` — is a design call, not this item.

items.title: NEW — the `[derive(Hashable)]` boundary cannot see a HAND-WRITTEN `impl .. with Hashable`: `is_hashable_type` reads scalars + `hashable_names` (derives and backed enums) only, so `[derive(Hashable)] struct Key { inner: Custom }` with `impl Custom with Hashable` is refused 'field `inner` … is `Custom`, which is not `Hashable`' — B289's class for Wire; it only rejects valid programs
items.discussion: rpc-34's F2 (2026-09-13); B319's `resolved_type_is_hashable` is the reusable check
items.body: `check_hashable_boundary` asks the impl table through `resolved_type_is_hashable`; pin the hand-written impl inside a derive and the missing-impl control.

items.title: NEW — the loader resolves a module's BODY FILE under two names: `import pkg::a::lib` resolves `a/lib.vl` a second time as the module `a::lib` (`submodules_in_directory` excludes `lib` deliberately; `resolve_module_file`/`longest_module_prefix` do not), so A67's rule had to skip `lib` by hand to avoid a second diagnostic for one root cause
items.body: `resolve_module_file` refuses (or aliases) `lib` as a segment when the directory is a module's body; one row or a silent alias — decide; pin `import pkg::a::lib::x` and `import pkg::a::x` agreeing.

items.title: NEW — after a STRUCT segment the import walk keeps the MODULE scope (a module-level `rem` in style.vl would shadow `Length::rem`, because the type's namespace is asked SECOND — B317 preserved every resolving path), while an ENUM segment REPLACES the scope with the variants; the two are inconsistent
items.body: Decide: a type segment replaces the walk's namespace (breaking for a path that resolved to a module member through a type-named prefix — census first) or the enum walk keeps the module scope too; pin the shadowing pair either way.
